newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: YPF PRESIDENT HEARTENED BY H1 PERFORMANCE.
newsitem.headline: YPF PRESIDENT HEARTENED BY H1 PERFORMANCE.

text.p: Argentina's YPF SA managed to turn a profit in the first half of the year despite a heavy income-tax and sales-cost burden, the energy company's president, Ricardo Monti, said Thursday.

Earlier YPF said its first-half net earnings rose 22.6 percent to 451 million pesos from 368 million pesos in the same period of 1996. In the second quarter, YPF's profit rose 1.8 percent to 227 million pesos from 223 million pesos.
Monti called the second quarter "successful" and said it was the second-most profitable three-month period since YPF was privatized by the Peronist government in 1993.
"In the first half of the year, and especially the second quarter, we made money despite having paid more income tax and despite increases in our sales costs," Monti said at a news conference.

Sales costs rose 2.5 percent in the quarter and 3.3 percent in the half-year because of the higher income tax burden, royalty payments and the depreciation of oil and gas reserves, reflecting stepped-up production.

YPF paid $800 million in income tax in the second quarter, and Monti estimated the annualized income tax bill would reach $3.2 billion. Until halfway through last year YPF was in credit with the state on income tax because of previous loss-making periods, but that credit has now run out.
"But the truth is that unit costs fell, because while total costs rose 2.5 percent in the second half, production expanded eight percent," said Monti.

YPF's natural gas output rose 13.6 percent in the quarter and oil output increased 4.1 percent. "In barrels, calculating the gas equivalent, we produced 7.5 percent more than in the same period of 1996," Monti said.
The YPF president declined to forecast second-half results, but said the company would not let up in its drive to keep costs down.
"We will be alive and kicking, just like we are now," said Monti.
